Thought: I need to determine the correct formula for the power index (PI) of explosives. The power index is calculated using the heat of explosion (Q_ex) and liberated volume of gas (V) of the explosive being tested, compared to the same properties of picric acid (PA) as a standard.

Looking at the options:
A. PI = (Q_ex·V)/(Q_ex,PA·V_PA)·50
B. PI = (Q_ex·V)/(Q_ex,PA·V_PA)·Q_ex
C. PI = (Q_ex·V)/(Q_ex,PA·V_PA)·100

The power index is typically expressed as a percentage, comparing the power of an explosive to the standard (picric acid). The basic formula would be the ratio of (Q_ex·V) for the explosive to (Q_ex,PA·V_PA) for picric acid. To express this as a percentage, we would multiply by 100.

Option A multiplies by 50, which doesn't give a proper percentage.
Option B multiplies by Q_ex again, which doesn't make sense dimensionally.
Option C multiplies by 100, which would give a percentage value.

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
